overview: This file combines a U.S. Embassy London despatch and three British economic-warfare enclosures concerning Japan’s wartime shortage of industrial diamonds with a separate State Department memorandum on Japanese ferrous metallurgy. The diamond correspondence assesses the limited output available from occupied Borneo and Java, the pre-occupation flooding of the Martapura fields and evacuation of diamond stocks, shortages of skilled cutters, and Japan’s inability to obtain anything close to the estimated 250,000–400,000 carats required annually by its war industries. The final document summarizes a Russian-language analysis concluding that shortages of ore, coal, scrap, and production facilities would prevent Japan, Korea, and Manchuria from substantially increasing their 1941 iron and steel output. Despite the file title’s reference to radium, none of the surviving documents concerns radium directly.

subfiles.title: Despatch No. 8900 on industrial diamonds for Japan
subfiles.from: Don C. Bliss, Acting Commercial Attaché, U.S. Embassy London
subfiles.about: Transmits British economic-warfare correspondence about industrial diamonds available to Japan from occupied Borneo and related supply questions.
subfiles.summary: Bliss forwards British Diamond Committee material on Borneo diamond production and Japan's wartime industrial requirements.

subfiles.title: Reading letter on Borneo diamond production and Japanese requirements
subfiles.from: J. L. Reading, Ministry of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Evaluates whether the occupied Martapura fields could supply a significant share of Japan’s industrial-diamond requirements.
subfiles.summary: Reading reports Borneo's tiny diamond output (2,287-4,219 carats) against Japan's estimated 250,000-400,000-carat need, doubting even a 30,000-carat wartime extreme-measures estimate.

subfiles.title: Owen letter conveying Larkins’s comments on diamond denial
subfiles.from: Rowland Owen, Office of the Minister of State, Cairo
subfiles.to: E. J. Holford-Strevens, Ministry of Economic Warfare
subfiles.about: Reports Larkins’s assessment of why Japan could not readily obtain or prepare industrial diamonds from occupied Southeast Asia.
subfiles.summary: Larkins credits flooding Martapura's fields and evacuating stocks for Japan's apparent diamond shortage, noting interned European cutters and blocked access by Japan's Surabaya consul.

subfiles.title: Larkins minute on Sumatra, Borneo, and Netherlands East Indies diamonds
subfiles.from: L. B. S. Larkins, Commercial Secretary, Cairo
subfiles.about: Comments on Japanese control of Sumatra and the availability, grading, and possible export of diamonds from occupied Java and Borneo.
subfiles.summary: Larkins doubts Japan can easily control eastern Sumatra given Aceh unrest, questions its expertise to grade Indies diamonds, and names possible remaining cutters, doubting Gutwirth would help given family ties to Allied territory.

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs memorandum on Japanese ferrous metallurgy
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, U.S. Department of State
subfiles.about: Summarizes a Russian-language article assessing wartime iron and steel production and resource constraints in Japan, Korea, and Manchuria.
subfiles.summary: Memo on a Kuibyshev despatch's translated article estimating 1941 Japan-Korea-Manchuria pig iron and steel output, concluding Japan lacks materials to significantly raise production above 1941 levels.

interest: Shows Allied efforts to deny Japan Borneo industrial diamonds via flooding, evacuation, and blocking Japanese buyers.
